name: Osteoporosis and low bone density
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> Osteoporosis or low bone density. Check question: Has a doctor told you that you have osteoporosis or low bone density (osteopenia), or have you ever broken a bone from a minor fall or lift? Yes, osteoporosis / Yes, osteopenia / Yes, fragility fracture / No. Safety question: Do you take warfarin-type blood thinners, an osteoporosis tablet or injection, have kidney disease or kidney stones, or have you had a recent fall or sudden back pain? (Yes: no automatic supplement hints; show talk to your doctor)

waterMl.notes: No change from the general FitPlate range (topic 30: 2,500 ml men, 2,000 ml women as drinks, est.). Osteoporosis alone does not change the target. With an oral bisphosphonate tablet the label says a full glass (about 180-240 ml) of plain water on an empty stomach and upright for at least 30 minutes. With kidney, heart or liver disease, pregnancy, a fluid limit or a diuretic show the general range only. Follow your doctor's advice.

conflictsWith.rule: Kidney profile wins on protein (0.8 g/kg per KDIGO info, no 1.0-1.2 g/kg push), potassium, phosphorus, calcium and vitamin D; supplements are the kidney team's (P13)

Do not cut dietary calcium (1,000-1,200 mg from food); calcium supplements doctor first and with meals; limit oxalate-rich spinach, chaulai and til; keep sodium low; P14 wins on oxalate and fluid advice
Same calcium target; use curd, paneer, buttermilk, lactose-free milk, ragi, til, greens and fortified milk; do not drop all dairy without a plan (P18)
Malabsorption and low bone density are linked; gluten-free calcium sources are ragi, rajgira and dairy; check wheat dishes; bone health, DEXA and supplements are doctor-led (P19)
Vitamin D treatment doses are doctor-set; P20 shows food and the 100 µg UL counter only (P12)
Keep calcium at least about 4 hours from levothyroxine; doctor manages thyroid dose (P9)
Same calcium target but harder to reach; ragi, til, low-oxalate greens, calcium-set tofu, fortified plant milk; supplements by doctor or dietitian (P34)
Oral bisphosphonate tablets can irritate the gullet; doctor review; antacid calcium counts toward the total; PPIs and fracture risk reviewed by the doctor (P17)

warnings: General information, not medical advice; the app does not diagnose osteopenia or osteoporosis
Fragility fracture, sudden back pain with height loss, repeated falls or a suspected hip fracture: see a doctor; hip fracture or spinal cord symptoms: emergency care
Never advise a calcium, vitamin D, vitamin K or magnesium dose; supplement doses and bone medicines are doctor-led
Total calcium from food and supplements should stay within 2,000 mg/day at age 51+ (NASEM, secondary); count antacids, Calcium + D3 and fortified foods
Do not stop denosumab or any bone medicine without the prescriber; oral bisphosphonates need plain water, empty stomach, upright for 30 minutes
Exercise for diagnosed osteoporosis needs doctor or physiotherapist clearance; avoid loaded forward bending and rapid or end-range twisting
Kidney disease, kidney stones, warfarin: kidney, stone and blood-thinner rules override (P13, P14, topic 4)
India-wide prevalence, ISBMR and BHOF values come from search summaries (secondary, unverified)
